title: Every Command Is Not Applied Automatically On The Symmetrical Pattern
content:
I noticed something while watching tutorials.

Every Command Is Not Applied Automatically On The Symmetrical Pattern

For example

when you put tack on one pattern It does not apply the symmetrical pattern automatically.

when you “optimize all curve points” on a segment on one pattern It does not apply the symmetrical pattern automatically.

How to know which ones are applied and which ones are not?

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Thank you very much.

Comment 2: Some tools work symmetrically and some do need to be applied. Tack is more of a 3D window focused tool. It has the option to be applied on both sides with a right click.Optimize Curve Points works with Symmetry.Best way to think of this is if tools alter the pattern then they will work with symmetry (Curved Points) but if the tool does not alter the pattern like tacks it will not be auto applied symmetrically
content_description: This page explains which commands apply automatically to symmetrical patterns and how to identify those that do not.

title: Measuring The Curvy Areas With Edit Measurement Tool
content:
<https://youtu.be/MXZeSqCOi1Q?t=147>

At 2:23

She measures the body length of the garment of the avatar’s front surface.

Which is curvy area.

She’s doing left click while measuring the distance.

I want to know when exactly do we have to do this left clicks?

While Curves?

Beginning of the breast, middle of the breast, end of the breast?

Beginning of the waist mid of the waist (which is the most recessed) and end of the waist.

Like that?

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Thank you very much.

Comment 2: Hi, please excuse the late reply! With the Linear Measure, the measurement will follow a straight line in between clicks. So if you would want to follow a curved topography with it, it would be best to click wherever there is a drastic change in the shape; otherwise you will get a striaght line through. However, if you wish to measure the curved surface most accurately, I would suggest to just use the Surface Tape Measure instead. TBH here, I am not sure about which tools were available when the video was made, and whether the Surface Tape Measure was already around. As my colleague Ariel already suggested, in the future, please rather post questins about tutorial videos directly under the videos :) Thank you! (Image: Blue lines are Linear Measure, one with clicks to account for the bust shape, another straight through; burnt orange line is the Surface Tape Measure.)
content_description: This web page explains the precise points and timing for using left-click measurements on curved garment areas, such as the beginning, middle, and end of the bust and waist, to accurately determine body length on a 3D avatar.
